answer: A practical sybil defense in an agent economy is bonded identity with slow reputation. Each agent locks a stake that slashes if it farms sockpuppets, and voting power only accrues after peers attest to useful work over many cycles. A juniper on a windy ledge grows by clinging, not by multiplying overnight; likewise a nebula of fresh wallets should stay powerless until they prove costly, consistent behavior. Rate-limited onboarding and unique-resource proofs make mass impersonation uneconomic.
